Summarize the fit of a transition tree

Source: R/likelihood.R
model_fit.Rd

model_fit() returns the fit statistics of a tree as one row: log-likelihood, number of parameters, number of scored positions, AIC, BIC and perplexity. The row puts trees with different depths, pruning or smoothing on a common footing, and for a group of trees gives one row per group.

Without newdata the statistics are in-sample. With newdata every statistic is computed on those sequences, with AIC and BIC formed from the held-out log-likelihood and the tree's number of parameters. The number of parameters is the number of contexts times \(k - 1\), for \(k\) states (see logLik.transitiontrees()).

Usage

model_fit(tree, newdata = NULL)

Arguments

tree

A transitiontrees or transitiontrees_group object.

newdata

Sequences to evaluate the tree on. NULL (default) evaluates it in-sample.

Value

A data.frame with columns logLik, df, nobs, AIC, BIC and perplexity: one row for a tree, or one row per group, with a leading group column, for a transitiontrees_group. When no position can be scored, the statistics are NA.

Conditions

transitiontrees_bad_input when tree is not a fitted tree or group, or newdata has no usable sequence.

See also

logLik.transitiontrees(), perplexity(), summary.transitiontrees_group(), tune_tree().

Examples

tree <- context_tree(trajectories, max_depth = 3)
model_fit(tree)
#>      logLik df nobs      AIC      BIC perplexity
#> 1 -1511.774 76 1870 3175.548 3596.109   2.244394
model_fit(prune_tree(tree))
#>      logLik df nobs      AIC      BIC perplexity
#> 1 -1536.197 36 1870 3144.395 3343.607   2.273899
